content_html: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation Tuesday banning the manufacture, exchange, distribution and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots for five years. "The law will take effect 90 days after signing, meaning the restrictions will not be in place during this year's holiday shopping season," reports FOX Chattanooga. "In the meantime, Hochul is encouraging parents and caregivers to consider potential safety and privacy risks before purchasing AI-powered toys for children." From the report: The legislation, S.9408A/A.11144B, applies to toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, including talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with children. [...] Under the new law, violators could face civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day for each violation, with enforcement handled by the New York Attorney General's Office. State Sen. Andrew Gounardes said the five-year moratorium will provide time to study the technology's impact on children and develop additional safety protections.
